question: Who was Ibn Turka?
proposition: Ibn Turka was a mystical philosopher: a Sufi-inflected scholastic between Tusi and Sadra, unobtrusively placed in the history of Iranian philosophy.
scholar: The de facto scholarly consensus, as characterized by Melvin-Koushki
reasoning: This is MK's own summary of the field ('such as it is'), which he says effectively obscures Ibn Turka's occultist project (pdf p.25); MK, not any single scholar, draws the line around a 'consensus'.

The consensus is traced to the Tamhid, to modern Iranian seminary curricula (pp.23, 454) and to earlier Western reference works that knew him thinly (pp.36-37); pre-modern readers offer mixed signals: the Safavid image 'appears' to have been that of a failed Sufi (p.453), while Afandi (d. 1130/1717) took him for a mystical philosopher of Shiʿi stock yet described the Mafahis as an occult work (p.26 n.25).
MK's objection is that it forgets what he treats as Ibn Turka's central work and that the man himself would have found the label 'cringe-inducing' (p.454).

MK is a partisan reporter and this is a construction of a field, not a position anyone in it holds in these words. Confidence records how fully the pages of MK's dissertation let us reconstruct this position and its grounds, not whether it is true.
